This file is the promotion payload, not evidence that `v0.4.0` is public.
Publication is established only by the immutable GitHub Release metadata and
its exact verified assets.

Veqtor v0.4.0 is a community-supported technical Alpha focused on bounded,
re-checkable paragraph history across local DOCX negotiation snapshots.

Highlights:

- the nine-tool MCP surface adds `trace_paragraph_history`, which captures one
  complete direct-DOCX candidate set and follows one selected paragraph through
  exact accepted/current or rejected-pending projection equality;
- history results include paragraph-scoped tracked-change units, explicit
  unresolved/ambiguous outcomes, closed resource limits, snapshot-bound `ph1`
  pagination and deterministic result/snapshot digests;
- `verify_quote` v2 can verify either accepted/current paragraph text or the
  bounded rejected-pending projection while historical `verification.v1`
  decision records remain readable;
- the server uses MCP Python SDK v2 and supports modern `2026-07-28` and legacy
  `2025-11-25` local stdio negotiation with the same `veqtor.mcp.v0.4` tool
  contract;
- privacy-minimized `paragraph_history.v1` and `verification.v2` compact
  records omit local paths and document wording while retaining the hashes and
  bounded summaries needed to re-check the result;
- the versioned macOS Claude Desktop Extension (`.mcpb`) contains all nine
  tools, the deterministic four-round demo and a history-first prompt;
- reproducible wheel, source archive and MCPB builds. `SHA256SUMS.txt` binds all
  three release payloads; the checksum is an integrity check, not a digital
  signature.

History is mechanical evidence, not semantic clause lineage. Filename or
explicit order is position-only and never verified chronology. Literal OOXML
metadata such as author string `53` is returned as document content but does
not establish a person, time, custody or intent. Veqtor does not infer that a
wording was introduced, deleted, restored, accepted or agreed.

MCP client request abandonment sends a cancellation notification and transport
teardown reaps the local server process, but synchronous tool work may still
finish and write its normal local provenance record. Cancellation is not a
guarantee that work stopped or that no local side effect occurred.

To install in Claude Desktop, download and open
`veqtor-mcp-0.4.0-macos.mcpb`, approve the extension, and enter the name that
Word should show as the author of new tracked changes. Then run the bundled
`try_veqtor_demo` prompt. The first activation may download a compatible Python
runtime and the dependencies pinned in `uv.lock` through Claude Desktop's UV
runtime.

For an optional advanced integrity check, compare the output of
`shasum -a 256 veqtor-mcp-0.4.0-macos.mcpb` with its entry in
`SHA256SUMS.txt`. The MCPB is not digitally signed. The v0.4 acceptance flow
tests a manual upgrade from immutable v0.3.0, rollback to v0.3.0 on a fresh
workspace, candidate reinstallation and complete uninstall. It does not claim
that v0.3 can read v0.4-only decision-record types.

Veqtor remains a local technical Alpha. It is not legal advice, a hosted
service, a full Word editor, a chronology/lineage proof system or a
tamper-evident audit log. Review the
[known limitations](https://github.com/JohnDeer-ai/veqtor-mcp/blob/v0.4.0/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md)
before using it on a real matter.
